outline.unique_angle: First-person frontline nurse opinion piece with a concrete time/word example (e.g. '90 seconds, three patients, three different opening lines'), framed for UK/AU/NZ privacy law rather than the US-centric HIPAA competitors. Top-3 are either pro-tooling vendor content, an executive compliance lens, or a dense academic study — none argue the personal, hand-drafted case from a working nurse's chair. The defensible wedge: pair the PMC finding that disclosed-AI satisfaction drops with a lived workflow showing the human line is worth the 90 seconds.

internal_link_note: Slugs taken from git log of published posts in this repo; both touch the 'where AI gets things subtly wrong / trust' theme and link naturally from the disclosure and accountability sections. warnings: AI Overview is present for the broad 'should nurses use AI' query and will steal clicks — only winnable with depth + a genuine first-person angle the Overview cannot synthesise.

Volume and KD numbers are ESTIMATES, not tool-pulled. Ubersuggest, Ahrefs KD checker and KeywordTool.io all required login / returned 404 on 2026-06-06, so no third-party volume figure could be cited per contract. Treat estimated_kd as directional only.

Top-3 SERP is high-DR (70/71/92) but NONE target the long-tail opinion phrase; the rough-formula KD (top10_avg_DR/5) overstates true difficulty for the long-tail because exact-match-title count is 0. Real difficulty for 'why I draft patient SMS reminders by hand' is low; difficulty to outrank PMC for the broad ethics term is high — target the long-tail.

YMYL/nurse content: needs RN byline + credential, a .gov or PubMed citation (use PMC11897835 disclosure-satisfaction finding), 'last reviewed' date, and no medical-advice phrasing — frame as 'in my practice'.
Competitors are US-centric (HIPAA/TCPA). Differentiate with UK NHS / AU Privacy Act / NZ framing for the target audience.
